Use case: scientific-educational. Create a richly annotated expanded teaching edition of PulseSensor back artwork. Image 1 is the exact submitted PCB geometry reference (green board). Image 2 is the approved black-and-white appearance direction (paired image). Make a large landscape 3:2 high-resolution teaching plate with a huge centered black PCB back and clear white silkscreen labels, surrounded by orderly verbose component callout cards on a white background. A small front-face inset may appear at bottom, unchanged heart and optical layout from image 2. Main title "PulseSensor • every component explained". Subtitle "Expanded back artwork study".
CRITICAL invariants: keep ALL physical parts in exact positions of IMAGE 1, exact counts. Especially the LED body at center and optical window on opposite face are FIXED. Do not move either. Keep JST at bottom and 5-pin amplifier at top. Image 2 lost some tiny resistors; use image 1 for actual component inventory. Black mask, white ink. No invented copper. Dotted leaders are explanation pointers, NOT electrical connections. Show mini dotted functional flow in separate footer: "LIGHT → SENSOR → FILTER → AMPLIFIER → SIGNAL". LED illumination is separate from electrical signal chain.
Every component must have reference and short function printed near it on the board, and more verbose external callout:
U2 top center: "U2 AMP"; external "U2 • MCP6001 op-amp / Amplifies the filtered pulse signal."
D2 upper left horizontal black diode: "D2 PROTECT"; external "D2 • Schottky diode / Series protection for sensor and amplifier supply."
C1 upper left inner brown vertical: "C1 FILTER"; external "C1 • 4.7 µF capacitor / Shunts the first filter node to ground."
C5 far left upper brown vertical: "C5 SUPPLY"; external "C5 • 2.2 µF capacitor / Smooths noise on the input supply."
R1 left of central LED, horizontal black resistor below C5: "R1 LED I"; external "R1 • LED current resistor / Limits LED current and sets brightness."
R2 lower left outer vertical black resistor: "R2 SENSE"; external "R2 • 12 kΩ resistor / Converts sensor output current to voltage."
C2 bottom left inner brown vertical: "C2 COUPLE"; external "C2 • 4.7 µF capacitor / Couples sensor changes into the filter."
D1 exact center rectangular white LED: "D1 GREEN LED"; external "D1 • Green LED / Shines through the fixed front aperture."
R6 upper right inner vertical black: "R6 FEEDBACK"; external "R6 • 3.3 MΩ resistor / Feeds output back to the amplifier input."
R4 upper right horizontal black: "R4 BIAS"; external "R4 • 100 kΩ resistor / Upper half of the reference-voltage divider."
R5 right upper outer vertical black: "R5 GAIN"; external "R5 • 10 kΩ resistor / Works with R6 to set amplifier gain."
C4 right middle horizontal brown: "C4 FILTER"; external "C4 • 2.2 µF capacitor / Couples the second filter node to the reference."
R3 lower right outer vertical black: "R3 BIAS"; external "R3 • 100 kΩ resistor / Lower half of the reference-voltage divider."
C3 bottom right inner brown vertical: "C3 COUPLE"; external "C3 • 4.7 µF capacitor / Couples the two filter nodes."
J1 bottom white connector: put text beside never on its body: "J1 POWER + OUT"; external "J1 • 3-pin JST-SH / Pin 1 Ground • Pin 2 Supply • Pin 3 Signal".
U1 is FRONT ONLY, not an extra back part: external small front inset callout "U1 • APDS-9008 light sensor / On the front: converts reflected light into current."
Use all 16 callouts once, no omission or repetition. Dotted leaders with precise endpoint dots to each physical part, separated cleanly, no leader mistaken for wiring. External cards may be grouped left 7 and right 7, U1 inset bottom left and J1 bottom right. Back can be huge to accommodate as much white on-board teaching ink as possible while respecting physical parts. Distinguish educational dotted pointers from actual underlying faint copper. Professional patient beginner-facing wording, legible typesetting, precise references and values.
Footer "VISUAL CONCEPT • EXPANDED FOR READING • SILKSCREEN FIT NOT YET VERIFIED". This is maximum-detail concept, not fabrication or validated wiring diagram.
